Raymond III Count of Tripoli was a member of the House of Châteauneuf and ruled as Count of Tripoli from 1157 until his death in 1183
He was the son of Raymond II Count of Tripoli and Helena of Armenia and succeeded his father at a young age
Raymond III was a minor when he inherited the county and his mother acted as regent until he came of age

*Early Life and Regency* was marked by the influence of his mother and the County of Tripoli's complex relationships with neighboring states
Raymond III's early life is not well documented but it is known that he was raised in a time of great turmoil in the region
The County of Tripoli was surrounded by powerful enemies including the Zengid dynasty and the Fatimid Caliphate

Raymond III played an important role in the politics of the Kingdom of Jerusalem and was a key player in the conflict between King Amalric I and the nobility
He opposed the king's plans to attack Fatimid Egypt and instead advocated for a more cautious approach
Raymond III's leadership was tested during the Siege of Tripoli in 1171 when the city was attacked by a combined force of Zengid and Fatimid troops

*The Siege of Tripoli* was a major turning point in Raymond III's reign and showcased his military leadership
The siege was eventually lifted but it marked the beginning of a long period of conflict between the County of Tripoli and the Zengid dynasty
Raymond III would go on to play a key role in the Battle of Hattin in 1187 although the exact nature of his involvement is disputed

Raymond III never married and died without an heir in 1183
*Succession Crisis* followed his death as the County of Tripoli was inherited by his nephew Bohemond IV of Antioch
The succession crisis marked the end of the House of Châteauneuf's rule in Tripoli and the beginning of a new era under the House of Poitou
